meta_description: Predictive maintenance across the fab — unplanned downtime down 37% and tool-availability reporting finally reconciled to one number

blocks.x: Predictive maintenance across the fab, unplanned downtime down 37% and tool-availability reporting finally reconciled to one number

Identity withheld, a semiconductor manufacturer whose fab measured losses in basis points of yield and whose maintenance ran on intervals the tools kept ignoring. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter quantified the intervals: 6.3% unplanned downtime on constraint tools, preventive maintenance consuming 11% of capacity regardless of actual condition, and three systems reporting three different availability numbers to three meetings.
Tool telemetry was rich but session-bound; failure precursors existed in the logs nobody had time to read. Engineering knowledge lived in shift handover notes.

We built the fab's maintenance spine: telemetry from constraint tools normalized into one condition model, precursor detection learned per subsystem with process engineers labeling confirmed failures, PM intervals moved to condition where the evidence allowed and stayed fixed where it did not, and one availability number reconciled across the systems that argued. The handover notes became structured evidence.

blocks.x: The reconcile-first pattern, one availability truth before any prediction, transfers to any fabscale operation; the precursor library is this fab's failure history and compounds with every labeled event. Another fab starts from its own handover notes.
Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
